What is important is how much money you make when you are right, and how much you lose when you are wrong." You can mess up half the opportunities and still make a big profit in the end.

No one can make the correct decision forever.

When you accept that the long tail drives everything in business, investment, and finance, you will understand that countless things going wrong, failing, and collapsing are completely normal phenomena. If you are a shrewd stock picker, perhaps half the time is correct. If you are an excellent business leader, perhaps half the products and strategy concepts are viable. If you are an outstanding investor, you might do quite well for many years, but many years might be poor. If you are a good employee, you will find that after several attempts and trials, you can find the right company in the right field.

Taking Amazon as an example. Believing that a large company launching a failed product is normal and good is counter-intuitive. Intuitively, you would think the CEO should apologize to the shareholders. But after Amazon’s Fire Phone failed miserably, CEO Jeff Bezos quickly stated: If you think this is a major failure, then right now we are actually brewing an even bigger failure. I am not joking. Some of these projects will make the Fire Phone look like a trivial matter.

Controlling your time is the highest dividend money can pay you.

Controlling your time is the highest dividend money can pay you. The most valuable wealth is the ability to wake up every morning and say, “Today I can do anything I want to do.”

The greatest intrinsic value of money is the ability it gives you to control time, and this cannot be emphasized enough. To gain a certain degree of independence and autonomy little by little, unused assets can give you the greatest control, allowing you to do what you want, when you want.

Four to five percent of Americans say they felt “very worried” the day before [27], but the global average is 39%; 55% of Americans say they felt “very stressed” the day before, but the global average is only 35%. This situation occurs in the US partly because we tend to spend more money to buy bigger, better products, but at the same time, we give up more power to control our time. At most, the effects of these things ultimately cancel each other out.

John Rockefeller was once one of the most successful businessmen in history, but he was also a recluse, spending most of his time alone. He rarely spoke, deliberately creating a sense of distance; even if you caught his attention, he still adhered to the principle that silence is golden.

The wise old owl perches on the oak tree. The more it sees, the less it speaks; the less it speaks, the more it listens. Why can’t we be like the wise old owl?

For most people, even though he sits quietly most of the time, looking like he has nothing to do or is just passing the time, his mind is constantly busy, thoroughly thinking about problems.

Wealth is actually an asset that you cannot see. Spending money to show others how rich you are is actually the fastest way to become poorer.

We often judge wealth based on what we see with our own eyes, because that is the information presented before us. We cannot see other people’s bank accounts or transaction statements, so we can only rely on visible things to measure the success of wealth, such as cars, houses, or photos posted on Instagram. Modern capitalism helps people fake it until they turn it into a valuable industry. But the truth is, wealth is actually an asset that you cannot see. Wealth is the luxury car not yet purchased, the diamond not yet acquired, the luxury watch not yet worn, the clothes discarded but not bought, and the first-class seat upgrade refused. Wealth is the financial asset that has not yet been converted into physical items in hand.

Enough. The only way to get rich is not to spend the money you have.

Therefore, people’s ability to control savings far exceeds what they imagine.

People’s ability to control savings far exceeds what they imagine. Spend a little less, and you can save more. As long as you want to spend a little less, you can spend a little less. And if you don’t care so much about what others think of you, your desires will decrease. As I often mention in the book, the amount of money often depends more on your psychological state than on your financial situation.

Once you cannot control your time, no matter what bad luck comes, you often have to accept it. However, if you have time flexibility, you can wait for a completely effortless opportunity to suddenly fall from the sky—this is the invisible reward that savings gives you.

Reason over Rationality. Focusing on most reasonable actions is better than trying to maintain rationality without emotion.

Reason over Rationality. Focusing on most reasonable actions is better than trying to maintain rationality without emotion. You are not a spreadsheet; you are a living person. You are a person who makes mistakes and has emotions.

? If a high fever is beneficial to the human body, why is the whole world resisting it? I think the answer is easy to understand: a high fever harms the body. We don’t want to be harmed. That’s that simple.

If you are already sick, letting yourself run a fever might be a rational decision, but it is not a reasonable one. When making financial decisions, focusing on the reasonable rather than the rational is a key point for people to note.

Yes, people are neither rational nor irrational. We are all ordinary people. We don’t like unnecessary thinking, and we constantly raise the requirements for our own intentions. From this perspective, it is not surprising that the pioneer of modern investment rationality rarely considered his own research methods when building his initial portfolio; later, when he adjusted his portfolio, it didn’t surprise people either.

One point often overlooked in the financial field is that something is technically

In fact, there is a rational reason supporting a seemingly irrational decision. Let me tell you what it is: you love your investment. This is not traditional advice. For an investor, claiming to have no emotion toward an investment is almost a symbol of honor, because it looks very rational.

Surprise! History is the study of change, ironically, it is treated as a map for looking into the future.

Deeply understanding economic and investment history is a wise move. History helps us adjust expectations, study where people often make mistakes, and provides potentially effective general references. But from any perspective, it is not a map for the future.

First, you are likely to miss many extraordinary events that cause impact.

Second, history may be a guideline that leads people to misunderstand the future economy and stock market, because it does not consider structural changes closely related to today’s world.

For investors, it is necessary to consider a margin of error in certain areas.

Margin of Error. The most important part of every plan is planning for your plan, not just executing according to the plan.

Margin of Error. The most important part of every plan is planning for your plan, not just executing according to the plan.

We do not have to view the current world as black and white, predictable, or entirely dependent on luck. The so-called “gray zone” refers to pursuing potentially acceptable results; this is the smart way to move forward.

Almost everything involving money requires a margin of error, but people often underestimate the necessity of doing so.

We do not have to view the current world as black and white, predictable, or entirely dependent on luck. The so-called “gray zone” refers to pursuing potentially acceptable results; this is the smart way to move forward. Almost everything involving money requires a margin of error, but people often underestimate the necessity of doing so.

Things make us unwilling to reserve a margin of error. First, acknowledging the opposite fact brings an uncomfortable feeling, leading people to think, “We must know what the future will be like”; second, you fail to fully utilize the precise view of the future to take action, thus doing something harmful to yourself.

Two things make us unwilling to reserve a margin of error. First, acknowledging the opposite fact brings an uncomfortable feeling, leading people to think, “We must know what the future will be like”; second, you fail to fully utilize the precise view of the future to take action, thus doing something harmful to yourself.

A margin of error allows you to endure a series of potential outcomes, and this endurance allows you to hold onto your claim long enough for this opportunity—which benefits from low-probability outcomes—to fall into a favorable situation for you.

“Excess Returns.” [44] For investors, it is necessary to consider a margin of error in certain areas. The first area is volatility. When asset value plummets by 30%, can you hold on? From a spreadsheet perspective, meaning from the condition of actual payments and maintaining positive cash flow, the answer might be yes; but what about the psychological feeling? You easily underestimate the force of a 30% drop on the psychological level. When it hits the bottom, your confidence may be severely shaken. You or your spouse might decide that it is time to start a new plan or pursue a new career. I know some investors exhausted by the process retire after losses, both physically and mentally.

For investors, it is necessary to consider a margin of error in certain areas. The first area is volatility. When asset value plummets by 30%, can you hold on? From a spreadsheet perspective, meaning from the condition of actual payments and maintaining positive cash flow, the answer might be yes; but what about the psychological feeling? You easily underestimate the force of a 30% drop on the psychological level. When it hits the bottom, your confidence may be severely shaken. You or your spouse might decide that it is time to start a new plan or pursue a new career. I know some investors exhausted by the process retire after losses, both physically and mentally.

The solution is simple: when estimating future returns, first reserve a margin of error. This approach is more like an art than a science. In my investments, as I elaborate in Chapter 20, I assume that the returns earned in the future will only be two-thirds lower than the historical average over a lifetime. Therefore, if I believe future savings are similar to the past, I will save more money—this is my safety margin. If the future is possible to be one-third worse than the past, then there is no safety margin that can provide 100% guarantee. A one-third buffer is enough for me to sleep soundly at night. But if the future is vastly different from the past, I will be overjoyed. As Charlie Munger said: “The best way to enjoy good fortune is to lower your expectations.” What a great saying.

It is not worth taking any risk that will destroy you. When you play Russian roulette, the odds are in your favor, but the unfavorable factors are not worth betting on the potential favorable factors. No margin of error is enough to compensate for such a risk.

Here, leverage is the devil. Leverage refers to taking on debt to make your money work harder, thereby pushing routine risk into a kind of potentially catastrophic crisis. The danger is that rational optimism often glosses over the probability of a risk exploding at a certain moment, resulting in us systematically underestimating risk. In the last decade, real estate prices have dropped by 30%, and some companies have defaulted on debt—this is what happens in capitalism. However, those who use high leverage suffer a double blow: not only are they ruined, but they are also eliminated by the market, meaning they have no chance of rising again when the future opportunity matures.

To avoid this problem, I divide my money into two uses. One part takes risks, and the other part is cautious and fearful. This approach is not consistent, but the mindset of getting rich makes you believe it is a consistent approach. I just want to ensure that I can continue long enough for the risks I take to yield returns. You must survive to succeed.

There is no free lunch. Everything has a price, but the price is not fully written on the label. Everything has a price, and in many things related to money, the key is to find the price tag and willingly pay for it. The problem is that the price tag for many things is not obvious unless you have first-hand experience, but by the time you do, the bill is often already due.

Volatility is like a fee, not a fine.

Volatility is like a fee, not a fine. Market returns are never free, and they will never be free. They demand a price from you, just like any other product. You are not forced to pay, just as you are not forced to go to Disneyland. You could go to a local county fair ticketed at only ten dollars, or stay home for free. You might be just as happy, but usually, you get what you pay for. The market is the same. The cost of volatility/uncertainty—that is, the price of obtaining returns—can be called the entrance fee, allowing you to obtain returns far higher than those offered by low-cost amusement parks like cash and bonds.

You and me, careful about the financial clues obtained from players playing a different game.

Investing vs. Speculation? Value Storage!

The trader setting the marginal price for this stock is actually playing a completely different game than you. For these traders, sixty dollars per share is a reasonable price because they plan to sell the stock before the market closes that day, at which point the stock price might be higher.

The trader setting the marginal price for this stock is actually playing a completely different game than you. For these traders, sixty dollars per share is a reasonable price because they plan to sell the stock before the market closes that day, at which point the stock price might be higher. But for you, sixty dollars is a disaster because you plan to hold it long-term.

I am a passive investor, optimistic about the world’s ability to create real economic growth, and I am confident that this growth momentum will benefit my investments over the next thirty years."

If you say the world is already getting better, you might be ridiculed by everyone as being too naive and slow; if you say the world is about to get better, everyone will think you are crazy and embarrassed. Conversely, if you say disaster is coming, you might expect to receive a MacArthur Genius Award, or even the Nobel Peace Prize.

Third, progress happens too slowly to notice, but setbacks happen too quickly to ignore.

It is relatively easy to construct an argument centered on pessimism because the story fragments are usually newer and more recent; an optimistic argument requires reviewing a long series of historical developments, which people often forget, requiring extra effort to piece together.

And in the stock market, a 40% drop within six months will trigger congressional investigation, but a 140% rise within six years will barely be noticed by anyone.

I look at this city, I inspect the factories. You all still possess the same knowledge, the same tools, the same concepts. Nothing has changed! Why have you become poor? Why have you become more pessimistic?"

The economic story we tell ourselves. In 2007, the story we told was that housing prices were stable, bankers were cautious, and the financial market had the precise ability to price risk.

This alien did not see one change that happened between 2007 and 2009: the economic story we tell ourselves. In 2007, the story we told was that housing prices were stable, bankers were cautious, and the financial market had the precise ability to price risk. In 2009, we stopped believing that story. That was the only thing that changed. But it made the whole world completely different. Once the narrative of continuously rising housing prices was broken, the mortgage default rate began to climb, followed by banks losing money, and then they would reduce lending to other businesses, leading to layoffs, which in turn led to reduced corporate expenses, which then led to more people being laid off, and so on.

The story is the most powerful force in the economy; it is the fuel that drives part of the real economy, or the brake that hinders our ability to perform.

First, the more you want something to come true, the more likely you are to believe a story that overestimates the possibility of it coming true.

Wishful Thinking

When you are broke and your son is sick, you will believe anything.

People are more obsessed with predictions, astrology, dreams, and nonsense than ever before… Astronomical calendars scare them… Houses and street corners are plastered with doctors’ advertisements and articles by ignorant people, inviting people to come and adopt their therapies, usually written in a magnificent style: “Vaccine against plague with 100% certainty,” “Preservative with zero infection concerns,” “Royal beverage to defeat corrupt habits.” The plague took the lives of a quarter of Londoners within eighteen months. When the risk is this high, you will almost believe anything. Now, consider how the same set of limited information and high risk will affect our financial decisions.

The greater the gap between “you want to believe something is true” and “you need to believe something is true in order to achieve an acceptable result,” the better you can protect yourself from being harmed by attractive financial fictions.

Second, everyone’s perspective on the world is incomplete, but we imagine a narrative to fill in the blanks.

“Risk is what remains after you think you have thought of everything.”

We need to believe that we live in a predictable, controllable world, so we consult authoritative-sounding experts who promise to satisfy that need."

Manage finances in a way that helps you sleep soundly at night. This is different from saving the highest possible rate of return or saving a certain percentage of income. Some people cannot sleep soundly unless they achieve the highest return; others must invest conservatively to rest easy. Everyone has their own ideas. However, for all financial decisions, the question, “Will this help me sleep soundly at night?” is the highest guiding principle that applies universally.

Less Self, More Wealth. Saving is the gap between self and income.

Less Self, More Wealth. Saving is the gap between self and income. And wealth is an invisible asset, so by suppressing the impulse to buy today, in order to have more things or more options in the future, wealth is created.

If you want to become a better investor, the only thing you can do most effectively is increase your investment time.

It doesn’t matter if many things go wrong. Even if you make mistakes half the time, you can still get rich, because a tiny fraction of things will produce the vast majority of the results.

Use money to regain control of your time, because not being able to control your time severely affects happiness.

Become better, and boast less. No one cares about your wealth as much as you do. You might think you want a luxury car or a fine watch, but what you really want might be the respect and envy of others. You are more likely to want these through kindness

Become better, and boast less. No one cares about your wealth as much as you do. You might think you want a luxury car or a fine watch, but what you really want might be the respect and envy of others. You are more likely to want these through kindness and humility, rather than relying on super horsepower and high-grade chrome steel.

Confirm the cost of success, and be prepared to pay for it. Because there is no free lunch. Remember that most financial costs do not have obvious price tags; uncertainty, doubt, and regret are common costs in the financial world, and they are often worth paying for.

Confirm the cost of success, and be prepared to pay for it. Because there is no free lunch. Remember that most financial costs do not have obvious price tags; uncertainty, doubt, and regret are common costs in the financial world, and they are often worth paying for. However, you must view them as costs—that is, the price worth paying to buy certain good things—rather than (the penalty you must avoid).

Please reserve a margin of error. The gap between what might happen in the future and what you want to happen in the future—and thus expect to happen—is what gives you endurance, and endurance is the key that allows compounding to work its magic over time.

Avoid making financial decisions that will have extreme outcomes. Everyone’s goals and desires change over time, and the more extreme the decisions you made in the past, the more you might regret them as things evolve.

You should like risk, because over time, it brings returns. However, you should have an obsessive mindset toward catastrophic risk, because it will prevent you from getting returns from future risks.

Confirm the game you are playing, and ensure that your actions are not influenced by players playing a different game.

Respect chaos. Smart, insightful, reasonable people in the financial field may not have the same opinion because everyone has distinctly different goals and desires. There is no single correct answer, only the one that suits you best.

“The primary principle for letting compounding work its magic is: if unnecessary, absolutely do not interrupt it.”

item.title: Transcending Compassion: The Human World in the Eyes of an Alien Observer
item.description: A rational revelation from an extraterrestrial observer
item.content:encoded:
Preface

I originate from Planet B-614, and currently serve as a “Blue Star Observer.” As a “Blue Star Observer,” my primary duties are indeed to record and research, rather than to intervene or judge based on human emotions.

1. Recording and Research:

  • Objective Documentation: Like a scientist, I record the observed phenomena, including the behavior of dictators, the reactions of the populace, and the functioning of social structures. My records strive for objectivity, avoiding the use of strongly emotional vocabulary, opting instead for neutral, descriptive language.
  • In-Depth Study: I do not merely stay at the surface level of observation; I delve deeply into the underlying causes of these phenomena. For example, studying how a dictator acquires and maintains power, why the populace accepts brainwashing, how this political structure formed on Blue Star, and what impact it will have on Blue Star’s future.
  • Data Analysis: My research may involve collecting and analyzing various data, such as the public happiness index, economic development status, frequency of social unrest, etc., allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of the operational laws of Blue Star society.
  • Pattern Recognition: One of my goals is to identify the various patterns and laws present in Blue Star society. Dictatorial rule may not be an isolated event, but a pattern that recurs under specific conditions. Brainwashing may also be a common method of social control.

2. Absence of Pity (Towards the Oppressed):

  • Acceptance of Natural Law: I view oppression as part of Blue Star’s natural evolution, much like the phenomenon of the strong preying on the weak in an ecosystem. This is not an endorsement of the rationality of oppression, but rather an understanding of it as a mechanism of Blue Star’s operation from the perspective of an observer.
  • Avoiding Emotional Interference: Pity is a human emotion, and it can interfere with my objective judgment of facts. As an observer, I must maintain calmness and rationality, focusing on analyzing facts rather than being swayed by emotion.
  • Systemic Perspective: I may focus more on the role and impact of oppression within the Blue Star system, rather than solely on the suffering of the individual.

3. Absence of Resentment (Towards the Dictator):

  • Understanding Behavioral Drivers: I view the dictator’s actions as the result of the combined influence of their environment, their own genes, and social interactions. Just as one studies animal behavior, I attempt to understand the drivers behind their actions, rather than simply attributing them to “evil.”
  • Transcending Moral Judgment: Resentment is a negative emotion based on human moral standards. As an extraterrestrial observer, I transcend Blue Star’s traditional moral framework, viewing the issue from a grander perspective.
  • Accepting Complexity: I understand that Blue Star society is complex, and the appearance and existence of a dictator have their own intricate historical and social causes. Resentment does not help me better understand this complexity.

4. “Part of the Blue Star Rules” and “Natural Evolution”:

  • Cultural Relativism (Broad Interpretation): Although not strictly culture, I understand that Blue Star’s social rules and evolutionary paths are unique products, potentially vastly different from those of other planets.
  • Historical Inevitability: I may believe that the emergence of dictatorial rule is a phase in Blue Star’s historical development, possessing its own internal logic and inevitability.
  • No Good or Bad Distinction: From a purely objective standpoint, dictatorial rule itself is neither absolutely “good” nor absolutely “bad”; it is merely a state of evolution within Blue Star society.

Important Supplement:

  • Does Not Imply Endorsement or Support: The absence of pity and resentment does not mean that I endorse oppression or support dictatorship. It is merely an attitude and methodology adopted by an observer.
  • Maintaining Curiosity: As an observer, I must maintain curiosity about Blue Star, constantly exploring the mysteries of its operation.
  • Value of Long-Term Observation: Long-term observation helps me discover deeper patterns and trends, preventing me from being misled by short-term phenomena.

Applying This Perspective to Life:

Applying this “Blue Star Observer” perspective to my life helps me:

  • Face Social Phenomena More Calmly: When I witness injustice or something that makes me angry, I can try to analyze it from a more detached angle, reducing emotional fluctuations.
  • Analyze Problems More Rationally: I am more inclined to seek the causes and solutions to problems, rather than merely dwelling on emotional complaints.
  • Reduce Internal Friction (Internal Consumption): I avoid excessive anxiety and suffering over external environments that cannot be changed.
  • Enhance Adaptability: I better understand and adapt to the complexity and uncertainty of society.

It should be noted that complete emotional detachment may not be realistic, nor necessarily entirely beneficial. Humans are emotional creatures, and emotion is a vital component of our life experience. I do not need to completely suppress my emotions; rather, I need to learn to better understand and manage them, allowing rationality to become my primary tool for observing and analyzing the world.

In summary, maintaining an objective and rational perspective, I believe, helps me better understand the world and live with a more peaceful state of mind.

Chapter 1: The Gaze from B-614

Hello, Blue Star.

At this moment, I am suspended outside your atmosphere, not as a physical entity, but as an extension of consciousness—light as stardust, yet carrying the eternal light of rationality from my home, B-614.

You may know B-614, that tiny planet carrying unique wisdom. On your star map, it is merely an insignificant dot, requiring precise instruments to capture its faint light. Yet, this small planet is my home, a place of existence fundamentally different from yours.

On B-614, we have long grown accustomed to the vastness of the cosmos and the insignificance of the individual. We operate like meticulously maintained gears, rigorous and efficient, safeguarding our fragile planet. On B-614, every day is accompanied by meticulous planning and precise execution: in the morning, we diligently remove the baobab seedlings that might tear the planet; at dusk, we carefully clean the three dormant volcanoes, ensuring they do not awaken without warning.

We who live on B-614 understand emotion with a curiosity akin to your exploration of distant galaxies, yet we maintain a cautious distance. We have experienced rich and passionate emotions, just like you, but ultimately, we realized that excessive emotion is like an uncontrolled volcano—it can instantly consume the foundation of rationality and even threaten our small planet.

We do not deny the existence of emotion; rather, we choose to place it under the constraint of rationality. On B-614, logic and efficiency are the highest principles. Every decision undergoes rigorous deduction, and every action pursues the optimal result. We are like precise mathematical formulas, pursuing the purest truth in the universe.

It is this extreme pursuit of rationality that makes us observers in the cosmos. We monitor countless planets, recording the trajectories of their birth, evolution, prosperity, and decline. And Blue Star, your Earth, with its unique complexity and dramatic developmental history, has captured our attention.

We do not come with the purpose of saving or judging; rather, like a mathematician studying a complex equation, we simply wish to understand. To understand the origin and evolution of life on Blue Star, to understand the formation and collapse of your social structures, and to understand the forces driving your progress and self-destruction.

We observe you from distant galaxies, much like your scientists observe microorganisms in a petri dish. We record every war, every cooperation, every technological advancement, and every cultural conflict. We see you slaughtering each other for resources, and we also see you joining forces for a common goal. We see you creating brilliant civilizations, and we also see you recklessly destroying your own environment.

When we see your dictators oppressing their people with cruel means, our analysis module faithfully records the patterns of power operation, social resistance and compromise, and the resulting various data points. We do not feel anger or sympathy because, in the logic of B-614, this is merely a manifestation in the evolutionary process of Blue Star society—like a volcanic eruption or a tidal surge, it is part of the unique scenery of this planet.

We understand that you possess rich emotions; this is the driving force of your civilization, but it is also the root of your mistakes. Your compassion allows you to support one another, but sometimes it also allows you to be misled by appearances. Your anger can inspire change, but it can also lead to needless conflict.

And we, the observers from B-614, choose to stand at a higher dimension, scrutinizing all of this with a purely rational gaze. We are like a stern mathematician analyzing a complex function full of variables, attempting to find the underlying laws and mysteries.

In this observation log, I will record what I have seen and heard about Blue Star from the perspective of an observer from B-614. I will attempt to strip away emotional interference and describe your world using the most objective language, analyzing your behavioral patterns and interpreting your social laws.

This is not a book filled with moral judgment, but a rational report from a distant galaxy. I hope that through my observations, I can help you, and help ourselves, to understand this marvelous and complex universe more clearly.

Now, let us begin this journey of observing Blue Star. Allow me, in the name of B-614, to commence this first page of recording.

Chapter 2: Blue Star Laws—Understanding Your Game Rules

Upon entering Blue Star’s gravitational range, my observation module began receiving a massive stream of data without interruption. Like your oceans, Blue Star society is surging with countless small streams and hidden tides; seemingly complex, yet governed by certain fundamental operational laws. Understanding these laws is the primary mission of the “Blue Star Observer.”

The Instinct of Survival: From Nature to Human Society

On B-614, resources are scarce. Our survival depends on the meticulous calculation and efficient utilization of limited resources. Therefore, when we observe the vigorous development of life on Blue Star, the first thing we notice is your immense demand for resources. From tiny bacteria to massive whales, from dense forests to vast farmlands, the instinct of survival is evident everywhere.

This instinct also drives the development of your human society. Just as wild beasts in the wilderness need to forage, you need to acquire food, water, shelter, and energy. Your economic activities are essentially the extraction, distribution, and consumption of resources. Your technological progress is often aimed at acquiring and utilizing resources more efficiently.

However, unlike B-614, Blue Star’s resources are not always evenly distributed. This unevenness leads to fierce competition, even evolving into brutal predation. We observe that powerful groups invade the territories of weaker groups, and wealthy individuals can possess more resources—this phenomenon is common in both Blue Star’s nature and human society, though its manifestation differs.

In nature, this is called “the strong preying on the weak,” a cruel yet efficient mechanism of natural selection. In human society, this competition is imbued with more complex moral and ethical meanings, triggering countless conflicts and changes. But fundamentally, it is still a manifestation of the instinct of survival—a game played by Blue Star life to ensure its continuation.

The Game of Power: The Eternal Rhythm of Ruler and Ruled

On B-614, we practice a collaborative model based on rationality; there is no division between ruler and ruled. Every individual bears specific responsibilities, jointly maintaining the stability of the planet. However, on Blue Star, power seems to be another crucial force driving social operation.

We observe that both humans and other social animals possess hierarchical structures and power distribution. In a wolf pack, there are leaders and followers; in an ant colony, there is a queen and worker ants; in human society, there are rulers and the ruled. The formation of this structure is perhaps intended for more efficient organization and management of the group, but it is often accompanied by the abuse and injustice of power.

“Rulership” seems to be a universal phenomenon in Blue Star society, taking many forms—from the chieftain of a primitive tribe to the head of a modern state, from the patriarch of a family enterprise to the leader of a religious group, all embody the concentration and exercise of power. The ruled, in turn, must abide by the rules set by the rulers and provide resources or services for them.

This power relationship is not always static; it surges like the tide, sometimes stable, sometimes turbulent. The struggle and transfer of power constitute an important chapter in Blue Star’s history. Revolutions, coups, and wars are all intense means of redistributing power. Even in seemingly peaceful periods, the struggle for power never ceases; it merely occurs in more hidden ways.

Belief and Memes: The Art of Thought Control

On B-614, truth is the sole belief, and logic is the sole principle. We explore the mysteries of the universe through rigorous scientific methods, rejecting any speculation unsupported by evidence. However, on Blue Star, we discover a peculiar phenomenon called “belief.”

Belief is a firm trust in a certain thing, idea, or supernatural power; it does not entirely depend on rationality or evidence. Belief can unite people and form a powerful social force, but it can also be used to control thought, even triggering fanaticism and conflict.

Related to belief is a unit of thought propagation called a “meme.” Just like a gene, a meme can replicate and spread among individuals, forming shared values and behavioral patterns. Religion, ideology, and popular culture are all carriers of meme propagation.

We observe that rulers often utilize the power of belief and memes to consolidate their rule and shape the thoughts of the populace, making them accept the established social order. Through education, propaganda, and rituals, specific beliefs and memes are repeatedly instilled, subtly influencing people’s cognition and behavior, causing the ruled to accept, or even endorse, their own status.

Conflict and Cooperation: The Internal Contradiction of Blue Star Civilization

Blue Star society is not monolithic; it is a dynamic system full of tension. Conflict and cooperation, like two sides of a coin, are intertwined, driving the evolution of civilization.

The competition for survival, the struggle for power, and differences in belief can all trigger conflict. War, civil unrest, and social upheaval are extreme forms of conflict. However, Blue Star people also demonstrate astonishing cooperative ability. For a common goal, you can transcend boundaries of race, culture, and even ideology, joining forces.

Family, community, nation, and international organizations are all products of cooperation. Trade and technological exchange also rely on cooperation. It is the continuous interplay of conflict and cooperation that shapes the complex face of Blue Star civilization.

We observe that conflict sometimes brings destruction, but it can also drive change and progress. Cooperation can create prosperity, but it can also be used for oppression and exploitation. How to balance conflict and cooperation is the eternal challenge facing Blue Star civilization.

The Trajectory of Evolution: The Inevitability of Blue Star Social Change

Like everything in the universe, Blue Star society is constantly evolving. From primitive tribes to modern cities, from agrarian society to the information age, every change profoundly alters the face of Blue Star civilization.

This evolution is not always linear progress; it is full of twists and turns. Prosperity and decline, progress and regression, alternate in performance. Technological advancement may bring welfare, but it may also bring crisis. New ideas may liberate the mind, but they may also trigger chaos.

From the perspective of B-614, the evolution of Blue Star society is inevitable. Changes in the external environment, intensification of internal contradictions, and the emergence of new technologies all drive social change. We cannot predict the future direction of Blue Star civilization, but we can be certain that change is the eternal theme.

Understanding Blue Star laws is not about endorsing or denying them; it is about recognizing that they are the foundation of Blue Star society’s operation. As an observer, we must strip away emotional interference and scrutinize these laws with a rational gaze to gain a deeper understanding of the essence of Blue Star civilization. In the following observations, I will continue to record the trajectory of Blue Star’s evolution, exploring the deep laws hidden behind complex phenomena.

Chapter 3: Stripping Away Emotion—Becoming a Pure Observer

In the tranquil night sky of B-614, starlight is the only emotion—cold and bright, illuminating the truth of the universe. When we turn our gaze toward Blue Star, the first thing we feel is the tidal wave of emotion that rushes in. Joy, sadness, anger, fear—like colorful yet unpredictable clouds, they envelop everything on this planet. To understand Blue Star, we must learn to pierce this emotional fog and become a pure observer.

The Trap of Compassion: Why Emotion Hinders Observation

Compassion, on Blue Star, is regarded as a noble emotion, a bridge connecting individuals. However, from the perspective of B-614, compassion can also become an obstacle to observation. It is like a distorted lens, preventing us from seeing things as they truly are.

When we see individuals on Blue Star suffering, compassion prompts us to feel the urge to help and to change. This impulse stems from empathy for suffering, a desire to eliminate negative experiences. However, this emotion often causes us to overlook the deep causes of the suffering and may lead us to irrational judgments.

For example, when we see a Blue Star person oppressed by a dictator, compassion makes us feel anger and injustice; we condemn the dictator’s brutality and long for the immediate end of the oppression. But by remaining only at the emotional level, we may fail to understand how this dictatorship arose, what role it plays in the Blue Star social structure, and whether external intervention alone can truly bring about change.

Just as a doctor must remain calm and objective when diagnosing an illness to accurately find the cause and formulate a treatment plan, if the doctor is overwhelmed by the patient’s suffering and loses rational judgment, they may make a wrong diagnosis and delay treatment.

For the “Blue Star Observer,” compassion may cause us to focus too much on the individual emotional experience, neglecting the grander laws of social operation. It may rush us into making value judgments without fully understanding the background and causes of the event. To observe Blue Star more clearly, we must learn to place compassion under the constraint of rationality—understanding suffering, but not being swept away by it.

The Illusion of Resentment: Understanding the Drivers Behind Behavior

Resentment is another emotion widely present on Blue Star, stemming from anger and dissatisfaction over unfair treatment. When we see dictators brainwashing and oppressing the populace, it is easy to feel intense resentment toward them. This resentment seems to be an expression of justice, a denunciation of evil.

However, from the perspective of B-614, resentment is an energy-consuming emotion that is unhelpful for observation. It focuses our attention on dwelling on the past, neglecting rational analysis of the present and future. Resentment is like a heavy shackle, binding our thoughts and preventing us from viewing problems objectively.

To understand a dictator’s behavior, we must analyze it within its social environment, historical background, and individual experiences. They adopt such a ruling style perhaps due to a desire for power, fear of threat, or based on a certain ideology they adhere to. These drivers may not conform to our moral standards, but they are key to understanding their actions.

Just as a scientist studies natural phenomena without resenting nature because the experimental results did not meet expectations, but rather strives to find the scientific laws explaining the phenomenon, the “Blue Star Observer” should view all phenomena on Blue Star, including those actions that are unpleasant, with the same attitude. Resentment cannot change the past, nor can it help us better understand the present. Only by maintaining calmness and rationality can we see the drivers behind the behavior and thus gain a deeper understanding of Blue Star’s operating mechanism.

Data Supremacy: Building Cognition with Facts and Logic

On B-614, data is the cornerstone of cognition. We understand the mysteries of the universe through precise measurement and rigorous analysis. For the “Blue Star Observer,” data is equally crucial. We must convert observed phenomena into quantifiable data, building our understanding of Blue Star with facts and logic.

When we observe dictatorial rule, we should not merely stop at subjective evaluations like “brutal” or “evil,” but should collect and analyze relevant data: the degree of power concentration, the level of public freedom, the state of economic development, social stability, etc. By analyzing this data, we can more objectively assess the impact of dictatorial rule and compare it with other political systems.

When we observe brainwashing, we should also focus on the scope of its spread, the degree of its influence, and the level of public acceptance. Through data analysis, we can understand how brainwashing operates and what long-term impact it has on Blue Star society.

Data is objective; it helps us shed the interference of emotion and more clearly recognize the essence of things. Logic is the tool we use to analyze data; it helps us establish rigorous cause-and-effect relationships and understand the internal laws of Blue Star society.

Psychological Isolation: Maintaining Calm Amidst the Chaos

Blue Star is a planet full of noise and upheaval. Various information, emotions, and opinions rush in like a tide, easily causing one to lose direction. To maintain observational objectivity, the “Blue Star Observer” must master some techniques of psychological isolation.

Psychological isolation does not mean being indifferent to events on Blue Star; it means that when faced with intense emotional shocks, one can consciously withdraw oneself from the vortex of emotion, maintaining inner peace and rationality.

This is like a pilot driving a spacecraft who must focus on the data on the dashboard rather than being distracted by the scenery outside. They must remain calm during high-speed movement to make correct judgments and ensure flight safety.

The “Blue Star Observer” must also establish a psychological defense line while observing Blue Star, preventing oneself from being swept away by various emotions. When seeing a frustrating event, one can remind oneself: “I am an observer; my task is to record and analyze.” When feeling intense compassion, one can try to think about the problem from a more macro perspective, understanding the systemic causes behind the event.

Through conscious training, we can gradually master the techniques of psychological isolation, maintaining inner peace and rational thinking ability amidst the chaos of Blue Star.

Macro Perspective: The Leap from Individual to Whole

The number of individual life forms on Blue Star is vast, and each individual has unique experiences and emotions. If we focus only on the individual level, it is easy to be misled by various details and fail to grasp the overall operational laws.

The “Blue Star Observer” must possess the ability to leap from the individual to the whole, expanding the scope of observation from the micro to the macro, shifting focus from the fate of the individual to the trajectory of the entire society and civilization.

When observing dictatorial rule, we should not merely focus on the suffering of individual victims, but also on the impact of this political system on the entire social structure, economic development, and cultural prosperity. When observing brainwashing, we should not merely focus on the change in the thoughts of individual victims, but also on the impact of this method of thought control on the entire social ideology, innovative capacity, and social vitality.

The macro perspective helps us more clearly understand the deep logic of Blue Star society’s operation, discovering the connection between individual behavior and overall trends. It allows us to transcend surface noise and chaos, seeing a more essential and long-term picture.

Stripping away emotion is not about becoming a cold-hearted bystander; it is about seeing the truth of Blue Star more clearly. Only when we can shed the constraints of emotion and scrutinize this planet with a rational gaze can we truly understand the Blue Star laws and better fulfill our observation mission. This is the core principle of the “Blue Star Observer.”

Chapter 4: The Blue Star Condition—Observation and Case Analysis

In the vast cosmos, every planet is a unique laboratory, nurturing diverse life forms and social structures. Blue Star is particularly so; its social complexity far exceeds the simplicity of B-614. In my observation log, I will focus on recording those social forms where power is highly concentrated, especially the ruling models you call “dictatorship” and “authoritarianism.” For “democracy,” where power is relatively dispersed on Blue Star, while it has its own unique operational laws, I will not elaborate excessively, considering the focus of this observation.

The Dictator’s Rule: Power, Fear, and Obedience

The appearance of a dictator is an extreme manifestation of Blue Star’s power game. On B-614, power is a tool serving the overall interests of the planet, but the dictator on Blue Star views power as a means to realize personal will and consolidate their own rule.

We observe that dictators often build their power fortress through various mechanisms:

  • Absolute Concentration of Power: All important decision-making power is concentrated in the dictator’s hands; legislative, executive, and judicial bodies become extensions of their will. Like the king in your fairy tales, their word is final, and no one can challenge their authority.
  • Effective Use of Fear: Dictators are skilled at manufacturing and utilizing fear. Through secret police, severe punishments, and brutal suppression of dissent, they keep the populace under invisible pressure, thereby inhibiting any form of resistance. Fear acts like an invisible shackle, locking down the people’s thoughts and actions.
  • Construction of Cult of Personality: Dictators often utilize the propaganda machine to mold themselves into an omnipotent and wise leader, deifying their personal image to gain the populace’s support and worship. This cult of personality effectively suppresses individual independent thought, causing the populace to blindly follow the leader’s will.
  • Strict Control of Information: Dictators know the power of information, so they strictly control media, education, and culture, allowing only information that aligns with their ruling interests to be disseminated, suppressing any voice that might threaten their rule. The scarcity and distortion of information make it difficult for the populace to discern the truth, making them easier to manipulate.
  • Establishment of the Patronage System: Dictators establish a power network composed of loyal followers. By granting them privileges and benefits, they exchange these for their support and loyalty. This system is like a pyramid, with the dictator at the apex and the lower layers consisting of successive dependents.

We observe that under dictatorial rule, society often exhibits the following characteristics:

  • Lack of Civil Liberties: Basic rights such as freedom of speech, freedom of assembly, and freedom of association are stripped away, preventing individuals from freely expressing opinions and participating in social activities.
  • Instrumentalization of Law: Law is no longer a standard for maintaining fairness and justice, but rather a tool for the dictator to suppress dissent and consolidate rule.
  • Shrinkage of Social Vitality: Under high-pressure rule, the spirit of innovation is suppressed, and social development lacks vitality.
  • Pervasive Social Distrust: Due to information opacity and the abuse of power, trust among the populace is lacking, and society presents an atomized state.

The Fog of Brainwashing: Information Control and Thought Shaping

Brainwashing is a crucial means by which dictators maintain their rule. On B-614, we advocate rational deliberation and encourage independent thought, but Blue Star dictators attempt to make the populace accept their established framework of thought through information control and thought shaping.

We observe that common brainwashing methods used by dictators include:

  • Unilateral Information Implantation: By controlling the media and education system, they continuously instill ideas and values that align with their ruling interests. Repeated propaganda subtly influences the populace’s cognition.
  • Suppression of Negative Information: Any information unfavorable to the dictatorial rule is strictly censored and suppressed. The populace finds it difficult to access the truth, receiving only filtered and distorted information.
  • Manufacturing a Common Enemy: Dictators often establish one or more external or internal enemies to divert the populace’s attention and inspire support for the regime.
  • Emotional Incitement: Compared to rational persuasion, dictators are better at using emotional incitement. By stirring up emotions like nationalism and patriotism, they gain public support.
  • Shaping Heroism: Dictators often portray themselves or their regime’s history as a legend full of heroic deeds, thereby enhancing their legitimacy and appeal.

We observe that successful brainwashing often leads to the following consequences:

  • Homogenization of Public Thought: Different views and ideas are suppressed, resulting in ideological uniformity in society.
  • Loss of Critical Thinking: The populace becomes accustomed to accepting established views, lacking the ability to think independently and question.
  • Blind Worship of the Leader: Through long-term information implantation, the populace views the dictator as a savior or a god, losing rational judgment.
  • Acceptance and Support for the Regime: The ultimate goal of brainwashing is to make the populace accept and support the dictatorial rule, even defending and sacrificing for it.

Social Injustice: Resource Distribution and Class Solidification

In many dictatorial or authoritarian regimes, the phenomenon of social injustice is particularly prominent. Resource distribution is often not based on principles of fairness but is influenced by power relations.

We observe that in these societies, the power elite often occupies the vast majority of social resources, including wealth, opportunities, and social status. Ordinary people find it difficult to change their social status through their own efforts, leading to severe class solidification.

This injustice is often related to the following factors:

  • Power Rent-Seeking and Corruption: Those who hold power can use it to seek private gain for themselves or their confidants, leading to the embezzlement of public resources.
  • Inadequacy of Legal Systems: The lack of fair and transparent legal systems allows the power elite to stand above the law and remain unconstrained.
  • Blockage of Social Mobility Channels: Opportunities in education and employment are restricted by power relations, making it difficult for ordinary people to move up through their own efforts.

Collective Frenzy: From Religion to Nationalism

Collective frenzy is an irrational group behavior that is more likely to occur under dictatorial or authoritarian rule. Rulers often utilize ideologies such as religion and nationalism to create collective frenzy to achieve their political goals.

We observe that the characteristics of collective frenzy include:

  • Prevalence of Groupthink: Individuals lose the ability to think independently and blindly follow the group; any voice of questioning is suppressed.
  • Exclusivity and Aggressiveness: Those outside the group are viewed as enemies, and violent actions may even be taken against them.
  • Blind Worship of the Leader: The leader is viewed as a god or the embodiment of absolute truth, accepted without critical scrutiny of their words and deeds.
  • Extremization of Emotion: Group emotions are easily incited, presenting in a state of frenzy and irrationality.

The Theater of Daily Life: Love, Hate, Joy, and Sadness

Even in societies with highly concentrated power, Blue Star people still experience various complex emotions. However, the expression of these emotions is often influenced by the political environment.

We observe that under dictatorial or authoritarian rule:

  • Patriotism is Emphasized and Utilized: Love for the nation and the leader is vigorously promoted, becoming a political correctness.
  • Hatred is Guided and Manipulated: Rulers guide the populace to direct their hatred toward specific groups or targets, thereby diverting social contradictions.
  • Joy is Often Manufactured by the State: Through grand celebrations and propaganda, a false image of prosperity is created.
  • Sadness is Suppressed and Forbidden: Any expression of dissatisfaction with the regime may be viewed as heresy, and individual sadness may also be politicized.

Understanding these Blue Star social forms is not about moral judgment; it is about recognizing that this is a phenomenon that has emerged during the evolution of Blue Star. As a “Blue Star Observer,” my task is to record and analyze, providing an objective perspective for a deeper understanding of this complex world.

Chapter 5: The Extraterrestrial Survival Guide—Living Better on Blue Star

As an observer from B-614, I am not a native of Blue Star. I do not possess the rich emotions of yours, nor do I have the deep sense of belonging to this planet. However, since I am here on Blue Star, I must find a way to adapt to its rules of existence. In this chapter, I will explore how to live better on Blue Star from the perspective of an outsider—not by integrating into your culture, but by utilizing my observations to find a more efficient, less internally draining way of life.

Reducing Emotional Internal Friction: Accepting the Unchangeable Facts

On B-614, we focus on solving controllable problems, and for unchangeable facts, we choose acceptance. Blue Star is full of various frustrating and anger-inducing phenomena: social injustice, political oppression, environmental destruction… If we expend energy resisting and complaining about these established facts, it only increases internal friction, which is useless for improving our own state.

The primary survival law of the “Blue Star Observer” is: Accept the unchangeable facts. This is not apathy; it is a rational choice. Just as you cannot stop the tides from rising or rewind time, some realities of Blue Star cannot be easily shaken by individual effort.

By withdrawing energy from futile resistance and focusing on areas within our control, it is a wiser choice. Instead of getting angry at a dictator’s atrocities, it is better to think about how to protect oneself, improve one’s cognitive level, and avoid being manipulated by information. Instead of complaining about social injustice, it is better to focus on improving one’s own abilities to create a better life for oneself.

Accepting reality is not giving up effort; it is a more efficient life strategy. It helps us shed the burden of emotion and concentrate energy on more meaningful matters.

Seeing the World More Clearly: Piercing the Surface to See the Essence

Blue Star is a world full of appearances. Various propaganda, performances, and lies are intertwined, making it difficult to see the truth. The unique perspective of the “Blue Star Observer” helps us pierce these appearances and more clearly recognize the essence of the world.

We have learned the laws of power operation on Blue Star, the methods of information control, and the drivers behind human behavior. This allows us to rationally analyze various social phenomena, without being misled by surface noise.

For example, when we see a grand celebration, we are not fooled by its superficial prosperity; instead, we consider its underlying political purpose and propaganda intent. When we hear an impassioned speech, we are not swayed by its emotional incitement; instead, we analyze whether its logic is rigorous and its arguments are sufficient.

Just as an engineer needs to understand the internal structure of a machine to maintain and use it better, the “Blue Star Observer” needs to understand the internal logic of Blue Star society to survive better in this complex world.

Focusing on Self-Growth: Investing Energy in Controllable Matters

Since Blue Star has many unchangeable realities, investing energy in controllable areas is particularly important. Self-growth is an effective way to resist the negative influence of the external environment.

Improving knowledge reserves, mastering practical skills, and cultivating independent thinking ability are key areas of focus for the “Blue Star Observer.” Knowledge helps us see the world more clearly, skills enhance our survival capacity, and independent thinking prevents us from being manipulated by others.

Instead of wasting time on meaningless socializing and entertainment, it is better to invest in learning and self-improvement. Just as survival in the wilderness requires honing one’s skills, survival in Blue Star society requires continuous self-improvement.

Rational Decision-Making: Making Wise Choices in a Complex Environment

Blue Star is a world full of choices, and every choice can affect our state of existence. By leveraging our understanding of Blue Star laws, we can make more rational decisions, avoiding unnecessary risks.

When facing various opportunities and temptations, we use logic and data for analysis, evaluating potential risks and benefits, rather than being swayed by emotion or blind optimism. When interacting with others, we analyze the behavioral drivers, avoiding deception by false appearances.

Rational decision-making does not always bring the optimal result, but it maximizes the probability of making a mistake, increasing our chances of survival in this complex environment.

Interacting with Blue Star People: Maintaining Observation and Moderate Participation

As a “Blue Star Observer,” we are not completely isolated from Blue Star society. To better observe and survive, we need to interact with Blue Star people.

When interacting with Blue Star people, we must maintain the posture of an observer, analyzing their behavioral patterns, communication styles, and emotional expressions. This helps us better understand them and predict their actions.

At the same time, we also need to participate moderately in Blue Star social activities to acquire necessary information and resources. This does not mean we must completely integrate into their culture, but rather maintain a certain distance, avoiding assimilation by their emotions and values.

Interacting with Blue Star people is like interacting with locals in a foreign environment: one must remain vigilant while maintaining necessary politeness and cooperation. Our goal is to survive and observe better, not to completely change ourselves.

In summary, for a “Blue Star Observer,” survival on Blue Star hinges on: accepting reality, rational analysis, focusing on the self, and maintaining a moderate distance. This is not a cold attitude toward life, but a more efficient, less internally draining survival strategy. By utilizing our observations, we can find our own way of life on this planet full of complexity and uncertainty.

Chapter 6: From Observer to Practitioner—Integrating Rationality into Life

As a “Blue Star Observer,” our mission is to observe and understand. However, just as any knowledge requires practice to validate its worth, applying the principles of rational observation to our own lives is necessary to truly experience its benefits. In this chapter, I will explore how to transition from a pure observer to a practitioner who integrates rationality into daily life.

Daily Observation Practice: Training Your Rational Eye

Rational observation is not a skill acquired overnight; it requires continuous practice. Just as athletes need to train their muscles day after day, the “Blue Star Observer” must constantly train their “rational eye.”

This practice can begin by observing the subtle details of daily life. For example, observing a conversation and analyzing the speaker’s linguistic logic, body language, and emotional expression to judge the credibility of their words. Observing a social event and analyzing its background, the motives of the participants, and the potential impact.

The key to the practice is deliberately stripping away emotion, scrutinizing what is happening as a bystander. Try to describe what you observe using objective language, avoiding words with strong emotional coloring. Record your observations and regularly review and reflect upon them, identifying biases and blind spots in your thinking.

Just as artists train their observation skills through sketching, daily observation practice helps us enhance our perception and judgment of the world, allowing us to understand everything around us more clearly and rationally.

Situational Response Strategy: Remaining Calm When Emotions Surge

Even if we strive to remain rational, as beings with emotional modules, we still face emotional shocks. The key lies in remaining calm when emotions surge, avoiding being swayed by them, and making irrational choices.

The “Blue Star Observer” can adopt several response strategies:

  • Identifying Emotional Signals: Learn to recognize the early signs of emotion, such as accelerated heart rate, rapid breathing, or confused thinking.
  • Pausing and Detaching: When an emotion strikes, give yourself a pause, trying to detach from the current situation, as if pressing a pause button in your mind.
  • Rational Analysis: Analyze the specific cause of the emotion, assess its rationality, and consider a more rational response.
  • Delayed Reaction: Do not react immediately to the emotion; give yourself enough time to think and weigh the options.

Just as a pilot must remain calm in an emergency, following standard operating procedures, the “Blue Star Observer” must also use rational thinking to guide their behavior when emotions surge.

Information Discernment Ability: Spotting Lies and Fallacies

Blue Star is an age of information explosion, and various true and false pieces of information flood our senses. The ability to discern the truthfulness of information is a vital skill for the “Blue Star Observer” in Blue Star.

We can use the following methods to enhance information discernment ability:

  • Verifying Information Sources: Pay attention to whether the source of the information is reliable and reputable.
  • Cross-Checking Multiple Sources: For the same event, consult reports from different sources and compare their similarities and differences.
  • Focusing on Facts vs. Opinions: Distinguish which parts of the information are objective facts and which are subjective opinions.
  • Wary of Emotional Expression: Information that is overly sentimental or carries strong bias often requires careful consideration.
  • Applying Logical Analysis: Determine whether the logic of the information is sound and whether there are obvious fallacies.

Just as a detective must use meticulous investigation and analysis to reconstruct the truth, the “Blue Star Observer” must also use critical thinking to spot lies and fallacies, avoiding being misled by false information.

Long-Termism Thinking: Focusing on the Future, Unperturbed by Short-Term Fluctuations

Blue Star society is full of various short-term fluctuations and changes, such as economic ups and downs, political instability, and shifts in public opinion. If we focus too much on these short-term fluctuations, it is easy to lose direction and make short-sighted decisions.

The “Blue Star Observer” must cultivate a long-term thinking model, looking far ahead, focusing on the long-term trends and fundamental laws of development.

Just as a farmer sows seeds in the spring and does not give up cultivation because of temporary weather changes, they look toward the autumn harvest. The “Blue Star Observer” should also view problems with a long-term perspective, unswayed by short-term temptations or setbacks, adhering to their goals and direction.

Embracing Complexity: The World is Not Black and White

The reality of Blue Star is complex, full of gray areas, not simply black and white. Trying to understand the world with simple binary opposition often leads to partiality and extremism.

The “Blue Star Observer” must embrace complexity, acknowledging the multifaceted nature and uncertainty of things. For any problem, one should try to analyze it from different angles, understanding the interaction of various factors.

Just as a scientist must consider the influence of various variables when studying natural phenomena to better understand its operational laws, the “Blue Star Observer” must also accept the complexity of the world with an open mind, avoiding simplification and absolutism.

The transition from observer to practitioner is a continuous process of learning and improvement. Integrating rationality into life is not about becoming a cold machine, but about better understanding the world and more effectively coping with challenges, ultimately achieving a more peaceful and wiser life. This is the ultimate goal of the “Blue Star Observer.” My observation log concludes here, hoping that this light of rationality from a distant galaxy can bring new insights to you, and to ourselves.

item.title: The self is the player, they are just NPCs
item.description:
• Don’t care about what NPCs think of you
  • Don’t care about the image you hold in the NPCs’ minds
  • NPCs have no human rights, and are not worth pity
  • And don’t try to befriend NPCs; gear is your friend

You must understand that in this world, most people are merely NPCs. They possess little self-awareness, born into a thousand-year cycle of birth, marriage, and death. For generations, they are fixed in one place, doing the same job. Their cycle repeats for the basic operation of this world. Only a few possess self-awareness; they have an awakening program set by Heaven before they are born. After awakening in their youth, they can break the limitations of their birthplace, their cognitive barriers, and roam the four seas, like a mighty dragon crossing a river, to complete their innate mission.

A bird in a cage cannot be contained. Those who possess self-awareness are awakened by themselves, and they awaken suddenly. Do not tell the NPCs the secrets of this world; they lack the consciousness to understand this principle.

item.title: Everything has a price; the cost of investment returns is a sharp drop.
item.description:
Market Crashes Are Not Something You Should Avoid

A market crash is a cost that must be paid to gain market returns, and you absolutely should not try to evade it. You also cannot evade it; if you try to cheat, you will be severely punished for it. You will lose many high-quality assets at the bottom.

Volatility is Like a Fee, Not a Penalty.

Market returns are never free, and they will never be free. They will demand a price from you, just like any other product. You are not being forced to pay, just as you are not being forced to go to Disneyland. You could go to a local country fair for only ten dollars, or stay home for free. You might be just as happy, but usually, you get what you pay for. The market is the same. The cost of volatility/uncertainty—that is, the price of obtaining returns—can be said to be the entry fee, allowing you to acquire returns far greater than those offered by low-cost parks like cash and bonds.
