Chapter 4: Narcissism. Earlier, we mentioned that a cult is a 0-100 spectrum. Narcissism is also a spectrum. In this regard, today, since I am not qualified to clinically diagnose whether a person is narcissistic, or a psychologist or psychiatrist. And I think psychology and psychiatry themselves have some problems. Why should they diagnose whether a person is narcissistic? That’s a later point.

So, today, the narcissism I’m talking about is just labeling. I am labeling narcissism on Scholar Mom, and on myself, and on many people who first enter this circle. Okay, let’s understand what narcissism is. Of course, everyone’s degree is different, but generally speaking, it is the inability to empathize with others. People are constantly… you see, the world is a dream, the world is a game, I am 100% responsible for everything, others are NPCs. This is a manifestation of the inability to empathize with others.

Then, not accepting criticism, not listening to criticism, not seeking help, because I am narcissistic; I know everything about myself, so why should I seek help? And always being in a superior position, and not reflecting. A large characteristic of narcissism is that I only focus on myself, and I hope you also pay attention to me. Then liking to show off, arrogance, and being busy with fame and profit, and beauty and the ideal partner—these are all manifestations of narcissism. And there is also the feeling that you are unique. Because your uniqueness also requires special treatment, and you feel worthy of special treatment. Look at the narcissistic people in life, for example, some bosses, or some people, they want you to be unique, they want you to break all the rules, and you must indulge them. In the spiritual world, we don’t share the same cosmic view and formal logic with those outside “Muggles.” Our universe favors people like us; we must be treated specially. We don’t work hard, we don’t strive, we can get money or a partner effortlessly. Others have to struggle hard. Look, this is a feeling of being unique, therefore worthy of special treatment.

The key point I want to talk about today is that most people think narcissism is this kind—we tentatively call it inflated narcissism. Actually, narcissism has another kind, which we call inferior narcissism. These two concepts were mentioned by Mark Manson, the author of The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fck*. This immediately answered many of my doubts.

Inflated narcissism is the kind we just mentioned. Inferior narcissism is, “I am so miserable! I went through so much trauma, the world owes me.” I am… look, the biggest common point with the previous one is that I feel unique, but not because I am capable, but because I am inferior. I, I, I am miserable, I, I am suffering, so I am unique. I am unique, so I deserve special treatment. Similarly, the universe must give special attention. I, I went through so much, endured so much suffering, experienced so much pain, I understood so many things, so I don’t want to work hard and exert effort anymore. I also want to effortlessly receive the universe’s generosity. Universe, give me your wallet quickly!

Look, inferior narcissism is also very common among people entering the spiritual world. Both types have many commonalities. They are all focused inward. When we have the mind-body-spirit discourse to support it, it is “I am the universe,” “I and the universe are one,” there is no duality. We are non-dualism. What is it called? Holographic universe. My big universe and my small universe are unified, so I am the universe, I am the universe. Doesn’t that make the inward focus even more reasonable? Just focus on yourself, let others cleanse themselves.

So, a cult is a slap on the palm doesn’t make a sound. Look, narcissism is also like this. People with inflated narcissism will always attract people with inferior narcissism, and the two form a codependent, a pathological symbiotic relationship. Moreover, narcissism is actually a healthy developmental stage. When a child is born, it has no outsiders. The more it completely focuses inward, the more it feels that the whole world should satisfy its needs. This is a healthy thing because it is through this that it forms its own independent personality, it meets its most basic needs. It can cry, it can throw a tantrum. This is what the omnipotent narcissism needs to do.

But slowly, through parental and social education, it can slowly learn that there are others outside. Not like the spiritual teachings say there is no one outside. There are others outside, and how should we get along with the people outside? So, how does a child… it develops from a healthy omnipotent narcissism into the kind of narcissism that many of us are stuck in. That is, the child might be in the stage of omnipotent narcissism, but is spoiled by the people at home, constantly narcissistic, and never dissipates. Look, a narcissistic child has a very big characteristic: they are very bossy. “This must be mine,” “That must be mine,” and “No, it can’t be.”

It actually builds a wall and hides its most vulnerable inner self. Because what is the most vulnerable thing for a child? It is being abandoned—that parents don’t like them, that they can’t eat, no one pays attention to them, no one touches them. These are the most basic needs. And a narcissistic child is always arrogant, very bossy. It slowly locks itself up, locks up its most vulnerable things. And if it grows up, and it habitually uses this arrogance to lock up its vulnerability, it will become an inflated narcissist. Similarly, if a child is not satisfied when it is young, and it is constantly in a state of scarcity, or a kind of narcissistic trauma, then it is not satisfied, and when it grows up, it constantly wants to compensate. Whether by seeking compensation from others, or by cultivating this, or by compensating itself, or it is also stuck in the process of constantly focusing on itself.

So, look, people with narcissism, whether they are the leader or us followers, hahaha, have a strong need for control on the surface. A need to be recognized, to be seen, to be comforted by the heart. But are these the biggest needs? No. These narcissistic people, whether they are any kind, and actually, all of us humans have another very important need, which we are unwilling to admit, and unwilling to point to: the tendency towards uncertainty, and thus accepting our existence, that is complex, uncertain, and uncontrollable. And merging with that fact, that reality. Look, we might not consider this a direct, explicit need most of the time, but every one of us has this need, especially narcissists, they put this need at the very bottom. If we honestly go to the bottom, to feel the ground we are standing on, it is actually unstable. All the philosophies, spiritualities, and various ideas that support us are actually unstable. They all have loopholes, they are all riddled with holes. All philosophical ideas are constantly compensating each other. After realizing this, your stable illusion collapses, the things you firmly believe in collapse. And that is what we need; that is what is closer to living in reality, stepping on the ground.

Feel it. And once you come into contact with it, just like we just talked about, the most abandoned thing for a baby is very vulnerable. As adults, when we feel this, damn, nothing is reliable. Of course, we can have some relatively reliable things, like partners or friends, but in an existential sense, these are uncertain, unstable.

Once you realize this, you won’t be so narcissistic. You might have a lot of mourning, a lot of sadness welling up, but that sadness is compassion, a compassion for all things, or for many people we coexist with, a compassion for the situation. Then you naturally care. “Hey, how is the climate now? Who is suffering in which place?” Even the news doesn’t focus on it, because the news focuses more on things that are fun or stimulating. You suddenly want to say, “Amidst so much uncertainty, I want to be a good person,” “I want to care about others.” So, earlier we said that avoiding joining a cult is about admitting that you have this tendency, and narcissism is also the same. First, we admit that we might be attracted by this idea—that I am unique, I must be treated specially. Narcissism is also the same. When we boldly admit, “I do have that part,” or “I have that impulse that the whole world must treat me specially,” “The universe must treat me specially,” we put this out first, and then you can even indulge, that is, let yourself think. After thinking about it for a while, you will feel that, “I am not special. The whole world, 10 or so people, 7 billion people, so many people are similar to me, and everyone lives in a similar context. I am not that special. My talents are not mine.” I occasionally read someone else’s book, get some inspiration, and it’s not that great. I have these things, but they cannot be the reason for me to be superior to others, to deserve special treatment.

So slowly, you first acknowledge, “I want to be treated specially,” and then slowly you feel, “I am not special, I am not special at all, I am just ordinary.” And ordinary—if you are narcissistic from the beginning, you are very afraid of ordinary. You are very afraid of mediocrity, very afraid of vulgarity. You want to be unconventional, you want to be bold. You want to research things that others don’t like or don’t pay attention to. You want to do counter-intuitive things. But slowly, when you accept that ordinary is also part of you, your life becomes very… it becomes simpler, very relaxed. You don’t need to constantly think, “I am different from those Muggles,” “I must create something to lead everyone,” or “I must constantly prove myself,” or “I must prove myself.” I am not proving myself. So, the cure for narcissism is ordinary—admitting that you are ordinary and mediocre.

Okay, we come to Chapter 5: The Age of Selling Magic. Haha, I myself used to like this term, and I liked to say, “I am a magician.” Today I have another little magic trick. Let’s talk about the modern ones first, a short history. For example, the ones we see today, with the law of attraction as the main core, everything that spread out—all the manifestation, Zero Limit, and One Thought Transformation from the last 20 years. They are all based on a core idea: focusing on the moving heart, focusing on your thoughts, and your thoughts determine many things, and staying positive. And if your negative thoughts, you must find a way to transform them, or cleanse them, or… well, ignore them, and you focus on what you want. This is the core of the law of attraction.

This system was proposed a few years ago, called Think and Grow Rich. Look, every decade, every 20 years, there will be a book that leads the trend for 20 years, 30 years, and it will sell tens of millions of copies. You think the law of attraction is the first? No, it’s been in the Bible for thousands of years, and it’s the best-selling. Then in the 30s, there was one called Think and Grow Rich. Do you see how similar it is to now? You must change the thoughts that hinder you from getting rich, and then you can become rich. Then in the 50s, there was The Power of Positive Thinking. And then after a while, in the 90s, there is Tony Robbins, the motivational master, right? He called it AWAKEN the giant within.

These books have similarities; they all became popular in the 20s, 30s, and 40s, and they constantly adapt to the context of the era. In the Think and Grow Rich book from the 30s, its entire historical background is that it was a Great Depression environment, the economy was very bad, and everyone wanted to get rich, but there was no way. Because it was a national capitalism, it naturally had a cycle of failure. And during that cycle, no one could find a cure. They could only wait for the cycle to pass.

But that book said that your positive thinking can make you rich, and how? That book became a huge hit, and 20 years later, it became WWII. After WWII, the baby boomers, many people returned to the family, and they wanted to achieve a modest life, how to return to the family, establish a good relationship, and at the same time earn more money to support the family. This is the main content and historical background of The Power of Positive Thinking.

Then in the 90s, neoliberalism rose. Most Western countries didn’t care about the individual anymore; if you didn’t do well, it was your own fault. This is the simplest version of neoliberalism. So Tony Robbins, that motivational master, came out. You can realize your highest potential. And it doesn’t matter if you are from a class; you don’t need to be a rich second generation; you can start from zero, and make yourself a millionaire, regardless of your education, your class, your cultural background.

This is the hope that Tony Robbins established for everyone. Look, it is also in the background of neoliberalism. Now, we are still in the background of neoliberalism, so the state welfare is absent, and the individual bears a lot of responsibility for taking care of themselves, taking care of the elderly, taking care of the children. So the law of attraction is great. Look, the law of attraction makes the individual responsibility not a heavy thing.

Zero Limit says 100% responsibility. Wow, if you put it in the context outside of spirituality, society already makes you 100% responsible for yourself, and it still makes you 100% responsible. But because this spiritual system first gives you a cosmic view, a worldview, you feel that you should be 100% responsible, that you should use your own thoughts to attract the life you want. How legitimate.

Look, the current generation of mind-body-spirit laws, besides the commonalities of focusing on what you want and focusing on the positive, it also has its own era characteristic: first, quantum physics has become a popular word, and almost all mind-body-spirit practitioners must use quantum physics to rationalize themselves, like the holographic universe, and the double-slit interference experiment.

Many people involved in things must understand this. It is used to support what? Quantum physics is used to support the observer influencing the observed. So, the world I observe can actually change like quantum physics. I can change it through the transformation of my thoughts, and the observed world will change. Damn it, this is nonsense. If you slightly tell this to a quantum physicist, he will almost go crazy. Quantum physics is a physical phenomenon in the microscopic world; it doesn’t affect our macroscopic world. No matter how you observe a phenomenon, it won’t change. Ugh. And also, you talk about the universe expanding infinitely, and the universe… look, did you notice? All mind-body-spirit things follow the most popular trends and scientific ideas of the present. They force themselves onto themselves, saying, “The universe is expanding infinitely, and our thinking, our own, is part of the universe, and we are also expanding infinitely.” To put it bluntly, money can also expand infinitely, our economy can also grow infinitely.

How does this sound so much like capitalism? Oh, so it is capitalism. This is a mind-body-spirit under the trend of capitalism, not a spiritual paradise beyond capitalism, but it is included in, or at least intertwined with, capitalism and neoliberalism. Ugh, I’m so angry. Just think, any of us, if we are not science majors, dare we casually quote something from bioengineering or chemical engineering? We don’t dare. We don’t dare to say something we don’t understand. But why is quantum physics so much? Why does everyone dare to say they understand a little bit of quantum physics? I am truly dead. Right? So, this is the first characteristic of the law of attraction today: quantum physics.

The second is the rise of social media. Look, before, the spread of knowledge was first carved on oracle bones, and then it needed to spread the gospel, so you had to go to school, and then you would be taught books and scriptures. Then slowly, you could publish, you could have your own views, and then there was television, then video. Now everyone can have their own official account, video, community. Everyone can have their own authority. So, the social media era is a highly narcissistic era.

And everyone feels, “The things I see are so similar to me. My worldview is like this.” And it matches the illusion we mentioned earlier: “I am the center of the universe, I am the only truly existing person in the universe, others are NPCs.” This high homogeneity of social media easily forms small circles. And people in small circles, we call it communities now, easily tend to be similar. And slowly, the different voices are initially accepted, and later they also start to converge, because of the pleasing mechanism and the belonging mechanism we mentioned earlier. So once the community becomes relatively closed, and especially the discourse in the community, the words you use, the language you use, the metaphors you use, start to become similar, the community starts to stagnate. I feel very sensitive to this matter; I am very sensitive to the stagnation of language. This is why a few years ago, when I was in academia, especially in gender studies, a small faction of feminists, I was very enthusiastic at first, and then I found, “Ugh, why do these people all speak the same way? I don’t want to listen anymore.” Then I felt that it was starting to become an old zombie. So I jumped out.

And now I have founded two communities: Circle in China, and Octopus Awakening. It also started to solidify. So I have left these two communities. And I am slowly exploring how to create more open and truly accommodating organizations for different opinions. I think my previous two communities were exploring this direction, but it seems that based on some structural reasons of the community, it still tends to homogenize. So this is a question mark that I keep holding. The third characteristic is consumerism becoming the driving force of manifestation. Look, in previous eras, it might be based on having to support the family, having to overcome the Great Depression. But now it is a crazy consumption, and market marketing, and various means, and various sales, and consumerism is rampant. And if you don’t criticize it, you can only follow it. Sometimes it even brings you benefits like honey, and you feel, “Hmm, I might still need some money,” or “I think it’s reasonable to spend on a five-star hotel or something.” “Others deserve it, why don’t I?” You start to feel that you must say these things. So consumerism is a big driving core of our contemporary mind-body-spirit.

So, why do you say mind-body-spirit is an industry? Well, if you look at the data, you know that in 2022, the entire mind-body-spirit industry, including yoga, meditation coaching, psychological counseling, various communities, and various more fringe spiritual retreats, totaled 43.7 billion US dollars.

You think about such a huge market, such a big slice of the pie. Everyone wants to share it, and everyone wants to ride on the imprint of this era, including what we might talk about in the future, about AI replacing human labor, about the fact that our life in this society has not much positive meaning. Capital likes these things? That’s combined with the social media we mentioned earlier, combined with the fact that our life is too uncertain, too without reliance.

Look, these things—capital, social media, the hope of certainty—will be generated. Mind-body-spirit, as an industry, constantly innovates, constantly replaces itself, self-repairs, and finds many of its own loopholes, and constantly optimizes itself to become a more self-consistent field. Look, our current astrology and human design can justify themselves, they cannot be falsified—these non-scientific things are particularly popular. I’m not saying science is good, it’s just that science, its premise is that it can be falsified. You can say today’s formula is wrong tomorrow, but astrology and human design can never be falsified. But what contemporary people need is something that cannot be falsified to give us a sense of certainty. Our life is too miserable, we are too uncomfortable, we need this.

I particularly like a quote from a YouTuber called Frog Dao Sheng. Because he himself was once a Christian, and then came out. And many people commented after his explanation, “If you don’t have a little faith, a little reliance, won’t you lose the meaning of life?” He has a quote that I particularly like: “If your spiritual world is too desolate, whether you believe in God or not is irrelevant.” In the end, it’s because you read too little. I think that’s it. You seek certainty, you seek meaning, the simplest way, the lazy way of not thinking, is to do astrology, to do human design.

If you read a little more, you can also find certain comfort in uncertainty, you can reconcile with uncertainty, and constantly overturn your ideas, constantly think. That is also a form of certainty. But this path is harder to walk. To be blunt, it is the path of the philosopher. The path of the philosopher requires privilege. What is the privilege of our current world? It is time, it is leisure time and energy. Most people, after working 996, where do they want to read books and think philosophically? They want to do some mind-body-spirit, and that can help them sleep. Then go to sleep, who goes to think? So that’s why mind-body-spirit is also a very good tool of governance. Everyone is busy working, and they casually use mind-body-spirit to soothe themselves. What a perfect social governance structure.

So, this leads to a very important point that I want to talk about: mind-body-spirit in the Chinese context is particularly toxic because it is completely depoliticized. I call it “Chinese-style mind-body-spirit capitalism.” What is politics? It is simple: the arrangement of public life. The politics we learned in primary school, it is called ideology. Why do we hate politics, don’t want to participate in politics? Because we haven’t had a positive experience of actively arranging public life. Even the smallest public life is politics, even if it is a neighborhood committee. But Chinese-style mind-body-spirit capitalism, it is based on consumption, and on love, it is completely depoliticized. Your family, and you return to the family, and you do wealth; politics is completely detached.

So, let’s go back to the development of spiritual earlier in the West. It has always been related to political demands. For example, in the peak period of the 60s, the hippie movement in the West, like The Beatles, and the Woodstock festival, they actually had demands, such as anti-war and social equality. In 2020, during the Trump-Biden election, there was even a spiritual writer called Marianne Williamson, who ran for president.

In a less extreme environment than China, actually, some schools of mind-body-spirit, because mind-body-spirit is a big concept, some are completely detached from politics, and some are willing to stand up to provide a new solution, a new idea for our politicization and political environment. For example, this Marianne, she feels that the current two factions are arguing too extremely, and they are very much in their own circles. We need a mind-body-spirit, a cosmic unity, but at the same time, we must have principles. Of course, she has a team. Of course, it’s not completely “everything is the best arrangement,” and she will stand up and say, “I hope mind-body-spirit can provide some solutions for politics.” So at least she has such an attempt. Although she eventually withdrew, hahaha.

But if we completely feel that mind-body-spirit is detached from politics, and from issues like feminism, environmentalism, labor, I think it is abnormal. It is not. If we belong to an interconnected society, then mind-body-spirit can naturally integrate with these things. But the version of mind-body-spirit that is most popular now, called “submission,” called “everything is the best arrangement,” called “everything is self-cleansing.” Wow, that is too easy to manage these people.

Okay, finally, how to cultivate critical thinking ability? Of course, this is a bit contradictory. If you have critical thinking ability, you don’t need me to teach you this chapter. But I will mention several points that I think are very important. First, read more books. You really need to read more books. Not just mind-body-spirit books, because I know there is a tendency in the mind-body-spirit field—if you look at your bookshelf, there are only mind-body-spirit books, then you really need to start reading more history, philosophy, more hard science, more empirical ones, and look for more independent news sources. And in hard science, if you are a liberal arts student and you don’t understand it, it doesn’t matter. You can flip through it, let your left brain get active. For a long time, your body is in it, your right brain is developed, but your left brain is not. This is a kind of overcorrection. Our mainstream society might be too developed in the left brain, and if you don’t understand it, it doesn’t matter. You can be permeated by its logic, its rigor, which is also a way to activate the left brain. And if you can slightly understand it with your brainpower, that’s even better.

And if you are really curious about quantum physics, you must read real quantum physics, not those fake spiritual quantum physics, pfft. Then you can also learn about basic philosophy, political science, anthropology, sociology, and logic, and linguistics—these things that understand the underlying structure of the human world. It will give you a framework, and you will know that when you hear a new thing, you can connect it with other knowledge. You won’t think, “Oh, this is amazing, it seems to be the truth.” You…

Our world has been around for thousands of years, so many philosophers, so many thinkers, step by step laid the foundation, and developed a little new idea based on the ideas of predecessors. How can you be so amazing that you can completely break away from their ideas and create your own new idea, and discover a cosmic truth? It’s not that simple. If you learn a little philosophy, history, and politics, you know these things are accumulated bit by bit. And besides reading these books, I also suggest everyone read useless books, because people in the personal growth circle love to read various technical, various… anyway, methods for self-improvement, it’s also an addiction. So you should read poetry, read sci-fi, read martial arts, read things that don’t improve yourself, to balance your information sources. Besides reading more books, the second point I want to talk about is colliding with people, debating more. Look, people in the mind-body-spirit field avoid debating because there is a kind of spiritual ego that says, “We are one,” “We are all unified,” “The world is harmonious.” Whatever you have, I can merge it into you, whatever you have, we can tolerate all emotions, all thoughts. So, in the end, this is a kind of enlightenment, a paste. It blurs things, and you feel that if you don’t think deeply, you feel that things can be compatible.

P—many things, you believe it can be compatible even if in the end, but the premise is that there is a huge rupture and many incompatibilities and dislikes. Only after debating, after fighting to the death, will they merge. This is Hegel’s idea of thesis and antithesis. First, you rupture, then you repair. Don’t be afraid of this rupture. People in the mind-body-spirit field are so afraid of rupture. How much are there? About the trauma of conflict. You pretend that you are especially harmonious, and you say, “I don’t mind, I, I don’t care if others criticize me, I don’t want to argue with people,” how noble you are, how elegant. I always feel that this is a band-aid. So, debating means solving it. It means you must first express it, like I am doing now, I am going crazy, I said a bunch of things. It doesn’t matter, don’t censor too much, just express it first. Of course, someone will disagree, and you can’t make everyone like you, and it’s okay if you are wrong, it’s okay if you are biased. Many of the things I said today are intentionally biased. I can’t make everything round, and I don’t want to do that. I just want to bring out my biased things, and welcome correction from me, welcome self-correction. I will slowly merge. Look at what I said today, I almost hate Scholar Cat. Of course, he has things that benefit me, this is not a justified hatred. I might slowly merge into it. Ugh, I don’t feel as angry as today. It might happen, but I can’t say, because it will happen. All these words I said today, I must say them. So you will find a very interesting thing: independent thinking is not achieved alone. Please remember this point: independent thinking is not achieved alone; it must be through collision. You must express it, and debate with people, discuss, explore, impact, friction, rupture, and then merge again. This is true independent thinking.

And this is the trap of our current mind-body-spirit generation: forcing every person back into their own small world, not caring about politics, not caring about others. Once your own logic is self-consistent, you don’t want to listen to other people’s logic, and you constantly self-cleanse, constantly self-reflect. You cannot recognize other aspects of society, you cannot view the world from the political perspective of other societies. It is a process that makes us lose the ability to think independently.

And the third point is that we must maintain a soft heart. What does soft mean? If you are narcissistic, you lock up your heart. Whether it is due to inferiority or arrogance, your soft part is locked up. So, to be soft means you will feel pain. Seeing a forest fire, seeing someone suffer, seeing a house collapse, you will feel pain. You just let that pain linger a little. Because I used to have a habit: when I see such painful news, I want to turn it off, I don’t want it to affect my mood for a long time. To a certain extent, this is the case. You cannot let it carry you away, and then you are depressed for the whole day, two days, three days. I think the method is to constantly learn how to adjust your nervous system so that it can coexist with this suffering, this pain in society, instead of just putting an ‘X’ on these pains and turning them off. Look, this is a very different path. When you close your heart, your heart becomes hard. That is your most precious thing; don’t defend yourself. So, one day, if you don’t feel pain when seeing these things, it’s not because you achieved enlightenment, or you achieved it, or you ascended to heaven. It’s because you cultivated it, you cultivated yourself to death.

If we say that very few people achieve enlightenment, this world is soft, and at the same time, it has a very strong place, and it can be regulated, but its hand is soft. It doesn’t lock itself up. When it sees separation and suffering, it still sheds tears. It’s not like, “I already know it is the universe’s operation principle, so these things won’t move me,” and I just cultivate myself, I cleanse myself.

Oh, this is also what they like to say: if there is war in the world, famine, strong suffering, hardship, then it must be that my unconscious, my inner self also has these things. And I must cleanse the desire or the memory and habit of fighting with others, fighting the war with others, then the world will be better. Pfft, damn it, I’m so angry. Right? So don’t cultivate it like this. If you cultivate it like this, you cultivate yourself to death. Ugh, this is also… I am not anxious, but my eunuch is anxious. Why be anxious? Look, if I say this pile of things, Scholar Cat will just smile calmly, he definitely won’t be angry, because anger is what a cultivated person would do. He would definitely say, “You are overthinking,” or look, you are like this suffering, he wouldn’t say anything, he would silently go back to cleanse it. And he would also make me cleanse it, if he still talks to me.

Anyway, today is my rambling self-talk, which is the end of my Deeply Loving Wealth. Why am I ending this blog? Because I feel that the atmosphere presented in the entire blog is a kind of… although I initially said I was an atheist, but slowly I have started to solidify my thinking. So, I think this podcast cannot continue. If I continue, I will still be talking about God, the universe, and so on. I think I’ve talked enough about those things, and those things definitely have some help. The many meditation audios before, many people feel they are helpful. If they are helpful, then they are helpful.

See you in a different Bubble.

Hahaha, hope that Bubble has more ventilation. Right? Because I cannot escape all bubbles. I just hope that whatever I do in the future is not so closed. By the way, if you don’t know, I have actually closed the Octopus Awakening community, so you can no longer join it. But Circle China is still there. I am not the main leader in it, but there are a few people I trust who are doing the main work, so I hope that if you are interested, you can play with Circle. It is relatively more open, and can accommodate different ideas. And if you like me, you can support me on Ai Fa Dian. Especially since I am in a transition period, I am brewing my new blog plan, or maybe other future projects. The hope is to break away from some of the drawbacks of the mind-body-spirit circle, but it might still accommodate some, because I have learned so much over the years, so I am still thinking about what form and what content it will be. So during this brewing period, I hope you can generously give me some financial support.

Recently, there hasn’t been too many cases, because I feel that in this period of change, I haven’t met new people. I hope to leave more white space for my own time, so that new ideas can emerge more freely. Just like I said earlier, the most luxurious and biggest privilege is time. And I am willing to give myself so much luxurious privilege. So if you are willing to support my process of independent thinking, I hope you can support me on Ai Fa Dian or directly find my donation QR code on the WeChat official account, and you can support me after any article.

Speaking of this, I think my current view of wealth is not just how many luxury goods you can buy, or how much liquidity you have today. I think it is being able to afford to be disliked—this is the greatest freedom. I can afford being disliked, I can afford public speaking—meaning I can afford to express my true views in public. I think this is the greatest wealth, including the time I just mentioned. Okay, so that’s all for today’s content. See you in the future. Bye-bye.

item.title: The victor suffers great depletion (or: The winner is severely wounded), the loser harbors revenge.
item.description: Victory achieved through military force cannot bring lasting success; the defeated will eventually retaliate. This has happened many times in human history, but these victories invariably turn into grave disasters—because the victory gained through force itself plants a seed of failure in the future, and the arrival of this failure is merely a matter of time.

item.title: Emotions make people stubborn (or resistant to advice/persuasion).
item.description: In times of disagreement and conflict, the one who remains calm is the strongest. Only this person can control everything, and calmness is the only way to prevent the conflict from escalating.

item.title: Not being contrary, not judging?
item.description: “Being contrarian and making judgments will never be effective,” the sage commented, “On the contrary, it will only exacerbate conflict. However, this is something that every person who tries to soothe others does unconsciously.”
item.content:encoded: “Being contrarian and making judgments will never be effective,” the sage commented, “On the contrary, it will only exacerbate conflict. However, this is something that every person who tries to soothe others does unconsciously.”

item.title: The Art of Communication: The Power of Questions
item.description: Exploring how to improve communication by asking questions, rather than forcing others to accept your viewpoint. A simple 'why' can change the direction of the conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Asking someone a question is giving them a chance to speak

The Cycle of Refusal and Explanation

When someone refuses to do something for us, our first reaction is usually to explain to them why they should accept our proposal. If the other party chooses not to concede, we often continue to explain, or present more arguments. We try to force others to accept through our own explanations, and the other party is doing the same thing. This is like a conversation between two deaf people: “No, because…”, “Yes, because…”, “No, because…”, “Yes, because…”, endlessly.

The Simple Word to Change the Dynamic

In fact, a simple word can turn this situation around—“Why.”

item.title: Listening to Others' Perspectives: Uncovering the Gold Mine in Dissenting Views
item.description: The article emphasized the importance of showing interest in others' perspectives during communication, and suggested that when faced with rejection, we should sincerely inquire about the reason to obtain valuable information.
item.content:encoded:
We are always eager to explain to others why they are wrong, but what we should actually be doing is showing interest in their opinions, and this also aligns with our own interests.

When others reject one of your proposals, you first need to show interest in the reasons behind it, and your attitude should be as sincere as possible. You can ask, “Why do you disagree?” (or “Why don’t you agree?”), and then listen carefully to their answer. Their answer is like a gold mine, containing many pieces of information worth pondering and utilizing. This is the secret.

item.title: I am you!
item.description: This article introduces six steps to avoid conflict escalation in communication, including calming one's own and others' emotions, understanding the other party's perspective, confirming understanding through restatement (or paraphrasing), using parallel phrasing to express personal views, and collaboratively finding solutions.
item.content:encoded:
Avoid getting caught in the cycle of explanation, threats, and personal attacks.

Step 1

Calm Your Own Emotions When we feel the impulse to attack the other person internally, we need to try our best to suppress it. For example, we can achieve this through several methods mentioned in the story: · Correcting misjudgments of facts; · Distracting yourself through deep breathing; · Or simply holding back the fist you want to throw; · Or any other method that might work. Every time you feel this impulse flare up during communication with someone, you need to review this step in your mind. Completing this step only takes a few seconds, and it is probably the hardest, yet most important, step. If you don’t have the impulse to attack the other person, that’s naturally even better. You can proceed directly to the next step.

Step 2

Calm the Other Person’s Emotions If the person you are talking to remains calm, it’s easy, and you can skip this step directly. But what if the other person is not calm? The answer is “do almost nothing,” or rather, “do almost nothing.” Especially don’t say to the other person, “Calm down!” or “Getting angry is useless!” At this time, you should follow the principle of “not contradicting, not judging.” Specifically, how do you achieve this? You can reply to the other person using words like “agree,” “okay,” “yes,” or “that’s right.” These words can convey the message to the other person: “What you are saying, and the way you choose to say it, naturally makes sense to you. I am willing to discuss this…”

Step 2: Calm the Other Person’s Emotions If the person you are talking to remains calm, it’s easy, and you can skip this step directly. But what if the other person is not calm? The answer is “do almost nothing,” or rather, “do almost nothing.” Especially don’t say to the other person, “Calm down!” or “Getting angry is useless!” At this time, you should follow the principle of “not contradicting, not judging.” Specifically, how do you achieve this? You can reply to the other person using words like “agree,” “okay,” “yes,” or “that’s right.” These words can convey the message to the other person: “What you are saying, and the way you choose to say it, naturally makes sense to you. I am willing to discuss this problem.”

By doing this, you will achieve an astonishing effect: the other person’s emotions will initially fluctuate, but then they will gradually stabilize until they slowly calm down. Achieving this step only requires the moment you say, “I agree.” If you successfully control your own emotions and successfully calm the other person’s emotions, you can proceed to the next step.

Step 3

Try to Understand Others Rather Than Letting Others Be Understood How do you achieve this step? The simplest method is “asking the other person questions.” The most effective question is: “Why do you disagree with my point of view?” After that, you must listen to their answer and try to look at the issue from their perspective, even putting yourself in their shoes and considering their interests. Strive to understand and accept others’ viewpoints, rather than imposing your own viewpoint on them. You must learn to find “consensus” between both parties in the words they use when explaining, and happily accept the other person’s viewpoint. This is a prerequisite for both parties reaching “consensus.” At this time, you should focus more on others’ “interests” (or “selfishness”): make yourself consider the other person’s interests more! Once you understand the other person’s thoughts, the solution will reveal itself, and the disagreement will be resolved easily. But usually, achieving this is not enough; you need to continue to complete the next step…

Step 4

By Restating the Other Person’s Words to Let Them Understand “That You Have Understood Their Viewpoint” If you want others to listen to your viewpoint, you first need them to speak. Then, use your own words to recount the viewpoint of the other person that you have understood. After that, ask the other person, “Did I get it right?” This will yield an unexpected magical effect—the other person will raise their eyebrows, show a satisfied smile, and exclaim, “That’s right!” Then they will fall silent and listen to you speak. Restating has two benefits: First, you can check whether you truly understood the other person’s viewpoint; Second, it lets your conversational partner know that they have been understood, thereby dispelling the thought of continuing the argument. However, there is a prerequisite for achieving this step—don’t let your previous efforts go down the drain just because you used the wrong word. This word is the keyword for the next step. The use of this word is also an art.

Step 5

Use Parallel Conjunctions to Present Your Viewpoint, Rather Than Pitting Two Opposing Views Against Each Other How do you achieve this? You can use the following words, for example: “As for me,” “For me,” “At the same time,” “From my perspective,” etc., instead of the extremely stiff “That’s right, but…” Then, after both parties have clearly stated the other person’s viewpoint, ask yourself, “How can the other person’s needs be met while simultaneously achieving my own goals?” By doing so, you can utilize the intelligence of both parties to seek a solution. Next, we begin to enter the sixth step.

Step 6

Propose Solutions Using Possible Win-Win Scenarios If we cannot find a feasible solution ourselves, try asking others if they have any good ideas. Then, we can discuss it together. If we cannot find any win-win method, we can use a compromise approach to solve the problem. People are often willing to accept a compromise because it at least establishes a friendly cooperative relationship. So, what if even a compromise solution doesn’t exist? This situation is very rare, but not impossible. At this time, you can negotiate with the other person and spend time together discussing possible ways out. Even if a solution is not ultimately found, at least a good relationship is maintained. And this positive relationship is crucial for achieving future collaboration.

item.title: Don't focus on money. You should focus on creating value
item.description: The less you want something, the less you’re thinking about it, the less you’re obsessing over it, the more you’re going to do it in a natural way. The more you’re going to do it for yourself. You’re going to do it in a way you’re good at, and you’re going to stick with it. The people around you will see the quality of your work is higher.

item.title: If they can train you to do it, then eventually they will train a computer to do it.
item.description: If someone can train other people how to do something, then they can replace you. If they can replace you, then they don’t have to pay you a lot. You want to know how to do something other people don’t know how to do at the time period when those skills are in demand.

item.title: You get rewarded by society for giving it what it wants and doesn’t know how to get elsewhere.
item.description: Think about what product or service society wants but does not yet know how to get. You want to become the person who delivers it and delivers it at scale. That is really the challenge of how to make money. Now, the problem is becoming good at whatever “it” is. It moves around from generation to generation, but a lot of it happens to be in technology.

item.title: Forget rich versus poor, white-collar versus blue. It’s now leveraged versus un-leveraged.
item.description: The most interesting and the most important form of leverage is the idea of products that have no marginal cost of replication. This is the new form of leverage. This was only invented in the last few hundred years. It started with the printing press. It accelerated with broadcast media, and now it’s really blown up with the internet and with coding. Now, you can multiply your efforts without involving other humans and without needing money from other humans.

This was only invented in the last few hundred years. It started with the printing press. It accelerated with broadcast media, and now it’s really blown up with the internet and with coding. Now, you can multiply your efforts without involving other humans and without needing money from other humans.

item.title: There are three broad classes of leverage
item.description: One form of leverage is labor—other humans working for you. It is the oldest form of leverage, and actually not a great one in the modern world. [1] I would argue this is the worst form of leverage that you could possibly use. Managing other people is incredibly messy. It requires tremendous leadership skills. You’re one short hop from a mutiny or getting eaten or torn apart by the mob. [78] Money is good as a form of leverage. It means every time you make a decision, you multiply it with money. [1] Capital is a trickier form of leverage to use. It’s more modern. It’s the one that people have used to get fabulously wealthy in the last century. It’s probably been the dominant form of leverage in the last century. You can see this by looking for the richest people. It’s bankers, politicians in corrupt countries who print money, essentially people who move large amounts of money around. If you look at the top of very large companies, outside of technology companies, in many, many large old companies, the CEO job is really a financial job. It scales very, very well. If you get good at managing capital, you can manage more and more capital much more easily than you can manage more and more people. The final form of leverage is brand new—the most democratic form. It is: “products with no marginal cost of replication.” This includes books, media, movies, and code. Code is probably the most powerful form of permissionless leverage. All you need is a computer—you don’t need anyone’s permission.

item.title: The leverage for ordinary people
item.description: Probably the most interesting thing to keep in mind about new forms of leverage is they are permissionless. They don’t require somebody else’s permission for you to use them or succeed. For labor leverage, somebody has to decide to follow you. For capital leverage, somebody has to give you money to invest or to turn into a product.

item.title: What is money?
item.description: If I do my job right, if I create value for society, society says, “Oh, thank you. We owe you something in the future for the work you did in the past. Here’s a little IOU. Let’s call that money.”

item.title: Play Long-Term Games with Long-Term People
item.description:
Compound interest is a very powerful concept. Compound interest applies to more than just compounding capital. Compounding capital is just the beginning.
Compound interest also happens in your reputation.
If you have a sterling reputation and you keep building it for decades upon decades, people will notice.
Your reputation will literally end up being thousands or tens of thousands of times more valuable than somebody else who was very talented but is not keeping the compound interest in reputation going.

item.title: Wealth is assets that earn while you sleep.
item.description:
Wealth is the thing you want. Wealth is
the factory, the robots, cranking out things. Wealth is the computer program that’s running at night, serving other customers. Wealth is even money in the bank that is being reinvested into other assets, and into other businesses. Even a house can be a form of wealth, because you can rent it out, although that’s probably a lower productivity use of land than some commercial enterprise.
So, my definition of wealth is much more businesses and assets that can earn while you sleep.

item.title: Find a Position of Leverage
item.description: I only really want to do things for their own sake. That is one definition of art. Whether it’s business, exercise, romance, friendship, whatever, I think the meaning of life is to do things for their own sake. Ironically, when you do things for their own sake, you create your best work. Even if you’re just trying to make money, you will actually be the most successful.

item.title: The limits of my language are the limits of my world.
item.description: Mental models are concepts that represent your understanding of how something in the world works. Think of driving a car: What do you expect when you press down on the right-side pedal? If the car slows down, you’ll be surprised—that pedal is supposed to be the accelerator. The accuracy of your model of the world determines your expectations, decisions, behavior, and—in the long run—your results.

item.title: Understand How Wealth Is Created
item.description:
It’s not really about hard work.
You can work in a restaurant eighty hours a week, and you’re not going to get rich.
Getting rich is about knowing what to do, who to do it with, and when to do it.
It is much more about understanding than purely hard work.
Yes, hard work matters, and you can’t skimp on it.
But it has to be directed in the right way.

item.title: Is the A-Q spirit a form of optimism and open-mindedness?
item.description:
A Q is a typical common man. His status is humble, and he lives in the rural society of the late Qing Dynasty and early Republican period. Through depicting A Q’s image and experiences, Lu Xun expresses his criticism of Chinese society at the time and his concern for the fate of the common people.

A Q’s spirit, also known as the “A Q Spirit,” is interpreted by some as a form of optimism and open-mindedness. When A Q suffers setbacks and bullying, he often maintains his self-esteem and confidence through a form of self-consolation. He uses self-deception and self-mockery to conceal his failures and humiliation, allowing him to find a psychological balance amidst adversity.
item.content:encoded:
A Q is a typical common man. His status is humble, and he lives in the rural society of the late Qing Dynasty and early Republican period. Through depicting A Q’s image and experiences, Lu Xun expresses his criticism of Chinese society at the time and his concern for the fate of the common people.

A Q’s spirit, also known as the “A Q Spirit,” is interpreted by some as a form of optimism and open-mindedness. When A Q suffers setbacks and bullying, he often maintains his self-esteem and confidence through a form of self-consolation. He uses self-deception and self-mockery to conceal his failures and humiliation, allowing him to find a psychological balance amidst adversity.

However, the A Q spirit is not true optimism and magnanimity, but rather an illusory psychological defense mechanism. A Q’s optimism is not based on an objective recognition of himself and social reality, but on the illusion of self-deception and self-mockery. This mental state allows him to cope with setbacks to a certain extent, but it also makes him lack the motivation to change reality and pursue genuine progress.

Overall, the A Q spirit in Lu Xun’s novels is depicted as a state of self-consolation and self-hypnosis. While it grants A Q a certain superficial optimism, it also reveals the predicament and helplessness of ordinary people within the social reality. It is not true optimism and open-mindedness, but rather an escape from reality and an illusory reaction to it.
